text:
li: FYI regression from nightly perf-run on 8xA100. steady-state loses comm/compute overlap. repro points to KV prefetch + cudaGraphs + small batcher windows. sharing timelines and logs. looking for root cause.

noah: can you paste the ncu timeline and the exact serving config (tp/pp, batcher window, seq distribution)?

li: config: TP=2, PP=2, microbatches=2, batch_size=48, seq_dist=[8:10%,128:70%,1024:20%], batcher_window=5ms, kv_prefetch=1, cuda_graphs=1, precision=fp16.

li: repro command (ci node g8):
```
export RW_KV_PREFETCH=1
export RW_USE_CUDA_GRAPHS=1
python perf_driver.py --tp 2 --pp 2 --seq-profile seq_profile.json --batch-window 5
```

li: ncu timeline excerpt (trimmed):
```
0.000: cudaGraph capture start stream=0
0.001: kernel=kv_prefetch_copy stream=5 (external)
0.003: graph_launch stream=0
0.005: kernel=fused_gemm_fp16 stream=0
0.010: ncclAllReduce ring stream=1 waiting on stream=5
0.011: cudaStreamSynchronize(host) // unexpected host sync during capture
0.012: kernel=fused_gemm_fp16 stream=0 (delayed)
```

maya: that host-side sync is suspicious. are we calling any cudaStreamSynchronize/cudaDeviceSynchronize in the capture path? or falling back to implicit sync because cross-stream work wasn't captured?

li: we don't call explicit synchronizes in forward path. kernel selector logs show different kernel choices per microbatch and a capture-cookie being written: 
```
KERNEL_SEL: microb=0 seq=1024 -> fused_gemm_fp16
KERNEL_SEL: microb=1 seq=8 -> gemm_fp16_tiled
CAPTURE: graph_id=742 write_cookie=0x7ff...
CAPTURE: external_streams=[5] // KV prefetch pinned to stream 5
```

sebastien: this matches a class of bugs: cudaGraph captures are per-stream and don't capture dependencies from other streams unless the dependency is recorded inside capture. If kv_prefetch uses stream 5 outside capture, graph_launch may block waiting for that data -> leads to host sync on some runtimes. We saw similar in an old NCCL+graphs issue.

noah: do we capture the prefetched memcpy into the graph? or is prefetch always issued before capture and assumed complete?

li: prefetch is issued on a dedicated async stream (stream 5) and we rely on event-sync to order against compute streams. But event recording happens outside capture. graph capture then records a wait on an event, which may not translate to device-side dependency and triggers host sync on launch on certain drivers.

jon: quick experiment idea: disable cuda graphs for the capture path or move the prefetch operations into the same stream that we capture. can you try running with RW_USE_CUDA_GRAPHS=0 and RW_KV_PREFETCH=1 to see if overlap returns?

li: ran that. with cudaGraphs=0 we get expected overlap and nccl AllReduce overlaps with gemm kernels. throughput up ~12%. so graphs seem to be the culprit.

maya: two hypotheses: 1) event-based synchronization between streams is converted to host synchronization when used with graph launch on this driver version; 2) kernel selection variability creates different capture shapes between microbatches, causing replay to inject stream syncs to preserve correctness.

sebastien: other angle: our kernel selector currently mutates a capture-plan object during selection and sometimes inserts a dummy cudaStreamSynchronize when it detects mixed-kernel capture shapes to avoid hazards. check selector diff from last green.

li: pushed diffs from last green: selector now emits an explicit "safety sync" if microbatch kernel choices differ across PP stages. that was intended to guard against mismatched temp buffer layouts.

noah: ah. combined effect: (A) safety sync insertion + (B) prefetch on external stream + (C) cudaGraph launch semantics. together they serialize. we should avoid bool safety sync during capture and instead prefer capture-consistent kernel paths or move prefetch into capture.

jon: pragmatic patch: if RW_USE_CUDA_GRAPHS=1 then force kv_prefetch to issue on capture stream (or as a captured memcpy). fallback: disable safety_sync insertion during capture and instead validate kernels prior to capture and choose a unified kernel variant.

li: filing a small PR to: 1) add env RW_PREFETCH_IN_CAPTURE=1 that switches kv prefetch stream; 2) short-circuit safety_sync when graphs enabled and kernels verified. will run CI perf job after.

infra-bot: CI job perf/nightly/graph-kv-216544 queued by li.

maya: also add a regression test: seq_dist skewed to a few very short and very long sequences with graphs on to catch mixed-kernel captures.

sebastien: good. also log explicit kernel-plan hash in capture metadata so replay can assert identical plan and avoid inserts.

li: thanks all. I'll open PR and attach ncu traces before/after. follow-up: if anyone has visibility into driver-level graph launch behavior for event->host sync, ping me. :pray:
